briefs.headline: Man City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield after Gravenberch red
briefs.summary: Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second yellow in the 62nd minute and Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored between the 65th and 78th. Andoni Iraola said the first booking 'is never a yellow card'; Liverpool are ninth.

briefs.headline: De Zerbi takes winless Tottenham to a Spain training camp
briefs.summary: Roberto De Zerbi said Saturday's 1-1 draw at Manchester United was 'the first time in this season we showed to be a team.' Spurs, without a win in six, train in Spain this week and host Coventry Monday, Oct. 19, at 3 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Burrow throws 4 TDs as Bengals beat Dolphins 31-24 in Miami
briefs.summary: Joe Burrow went 23 of 32 for 190 yards with scoring passes to Mike Gesicki, Samaje Perine, Tanner Hudson and Ja'Marr Chase, and Jordan Battle intercepted Malik Willis twice. Cincinnati is 3-2 and has its bye this week.

briefs.headline: Jets beat Browns 17-12 in the rain after a mishandled punt snap
briefs.summary: Denzel Boston's 29-yard catch from Deshaun Watson put Cleveland ahead 12-10 with 6:15 left, then punter Corey Bojorquez mishandled a snap and Braelon Allen ran 22 yards for the winner. The Browns had a season-low 198 yards and are 3-2.

briefs.headline: Rodriguez calls WVU defense his most frustrating as a head coach
briefs.summary: Rich Rodriguez said the defense that allowed 482 yards in Arizona's 52-31 win Saturday has him 'as frustrated as I've ever been as a head coach with one side of the ball.' Cincinnati visits Saturday at noon ET.

briefs.headline: Turang homers, Brewers beat Dodgers 2-1 in NLCS opener
briefs.summary: Brice Turang homered off Tarik Skubal and Luis Lara's fifth-inning single broke a tie Sunday in Milwaukee; the bullpen allowed two hits after Jacob Misiorowski left, and Los Angeles went 1 for 6 with runners on. Game 2 is Monday, 5 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Griffin faces Rasmussen as ALCS opens Monday in St. Petersburg
briefs.summary: Cleveland starts Foster Griffin, a 15-game winner with a 3.60 ERA, against Drew Rasmussen, 16 wins and a 2.67 ERA, at 8 p.m. ET on TBS; the Rays won five of the six regular-season meetings.

briefs.headline: Little's 57-yarder as time expires beats Eagles 19-17 in London
briefs.summary: Cam Little kicked it after Ameer Abdullah's 53-yard kickoff return left one second Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium; Philadelphia, without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, ran for 22 yards and has lost three of five.

briefs.headline: Purdy's two late drives lift 49ers past Seahawks 32-29
briefs.summary: Brock Purdy found Mike Evans repeatedly on the go-ahead drive and Eddy Pineiro's 43-yard field goal with 1:56 left finished it Sunday in Seattle; the game had seven turnovers and an ejection, and San Francisco is unbeaten in five.

briefs.headline: Huntley's sneak in OT lifts Ravens over Falcons 30-23
briefs.summary: Filling in for Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley led a tying touchdown and 2-point conversion in the last minute Sunday night in Atlanta, then scored from the 1; Kyle Hamilton's interception ended it. Baltimore leads the AFC North alone.

briefs.headline: Georgia takes over No. 1 in the AP poll; Texas drops to 7th
briefs.summary: The Bulldogs drew 66 first-place votes Sunday after beating Alabama, with Notre Dame, Miami, Ohio State and Indiana behind them; Texas fell six places after losing to Oklahoma, UCLA climbed nine spots to 12th and Kentucky entered at 15th.

briefs.headline: Rangers rout Canucks 6-2 in first game without Shesterkin
briefs.summary: Ty Kartye and Will Cuylle scored twice each Sunday at Madison Square Garden and Dylan Garand, 24, made 19 saves in his first start since Igor Shesterkin was lost for the season with a right knee injury; New York has won all four home games.

briefs.headline: Hurricanes beat Flyers 4-1, a record seventh straight loss to open
briefs.summary: Andrei Svechnikov and Sebastian Aho each had a goal and an assist Sunday in Philadelphia, where rookie defenseman Oliver Bonk figured in three Carolina goals in his debut; no Flyers team had opened a season with seven straight losses.

briefs.headline: Palace beats Forest 3-1 to spoil Glasner's return to Selhurst
briefs.summary: Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino answered Dan Ndoye's third-minute goal Sunday, Pierre Sage's first home league win since replacing Oliver Glasner, who left for Nottingham Forest in the summer.

briefs.headline: Verstappen wins in Singapore at the 10th attempt, Antonelli third
briefs.summary: Max Verstappen led every lap from pole Sunday at Marina Bay for his 73rd win on his 250th start, 7.3 seconds clear of Charles Leclerc; Kimi Antonelli's third extended his championship lead, and Lewis Hamilton's strategy call left him sixth.

briefs.headline: Onosato returns home to Ishikawa as the jungyo reaches Kanazawa
briefs.summary: The yokozuna (grand champion), September's yusho (championship) winner, did butsukari (pushing drills) and kids' sumo Monday at the jungyo (regional tour) stop in his home prefecture. The Kyushu basho (tournament) opens Nov. 8, 27 days out.

briefs.headline: Aonishiki resumes pushing drills with the left ankle taped
briefs.summary: The ozeki (champion, second-highest rank) did his first butsukari (pushing drills) of the tour Sunday at Imizu, the ankle taped rather than in a tabi (split-toed sock), against sekiwake Fujinokawa; he called the feel "still a long way off."

sections.label: On the Water
sections.note: All four waters reported from the locked fishing.json, generated_at 2026-10-12T05:44:21-04:00, errors list empty; the file was not re-run by this desk and every figure is printed as it stands there. The Williams River blew out Sunday afternoon: 1,340 cfs and 4.24 feet at 5:15 a.m. against 47.6 cfs and 1.28 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark, on a USGS 03186500 two-day trace pulled at 5:48 a.m.; the fetcher's 48.8 and 1.29 comparison is again the first point of its two-day window, the 6 a.m. Saturday reading, so its rising flags are right on the day and the trace, not the comparison, carries the timeline. The river held 45.3 to 48.8 cfs through Saturday and Sunday dawn, crept to 50.0 at 8:30 a.m. Sunday, 51.2 at 9:45, 62.8 by 1:15 p.m., then went to 128 at 2 p.m., 809 at 2:15, 1,010 at 3 p.m., 2,080 at 5:30 and a peak so far of 2,430 cfs and 5.51 feet at 7 and 7:15 p.m. Sunday, and has receded since, 1,740 at midnight, 1,340 at 3:45 a.m., and 1,320 to 1,340 cfs between 4 and 5:15 a.m., the recession flattening in the last hour. The Gauley near Craigsville (03189100), above Summersville Lake, rose from 198 cfs at 2 p.m. Sunday to 711 at 3 p.m., 1,310 at 8 p.m., 3,420 at midnight and a peak of 3,940 cfs and 13.57 feet at 2:45 a.m., 3,820 cfs and 13.52 feet at 5:30 a.m. 03189600 below Summersville Dam, stage only (its discharge series again carried no values), held 11.00 to 11.07 feet through the whole window, 11.05 at 4:45 a.m., the release unchanged on the trace. The Gauley above Belva (03192000) ran 2,690 cfs at 5 a.m. Sunday, 2,770 through midday, 2,880 at 7 p.m., 3,910 at 11 p.m., 4,690 at midnight, a peak of 5,000 cfs and 5.38 feet at 1 a.m., and 4,470 cfs and 5.10 feet at 5 a.m., so the rise below the dam is tributary water, not a release change on the trace. All of that is a reading of USGS traces, not a Corps statement; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened. NWS: api.weather.gov's active list for West Virginia carried zero products at 5:48 a.m., so no flood watch, warning or advisory covers the Gauley, Elk or Williams this morning; the Wind Advisories of Sunday have expired. Ohio: Point Pleasant 26.03 feet at 5 a.m., fetcher's rising flag right on the day, up 0.94 from 25.09 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark, with the 24.53 comparison the first point of the window (24.53 at 6 a.m. Saturday on this pull) making it look like 1.50; the window high was 26.15 at 4:15 a.m. and the gauge eased to 26.03 by 5. Huntington 28.01 feet at 5 a.m., rising flag right on the day and at the hour, up 1.94 from 26.07 at 5 a.m. Sunday, every hourly reading higher than the last since 7 p.m. and 28.01 the window high; the fetcher's 25.5 is the first point of the window (25.51 at 6 a.m. Saturday) and makes it look like 2.51. For Coastal Pender (NCZ106) api.weather.gov carried zero products at 5:48 a.m., and the five active products statewide in North Carolina are all NWS Greenville-Spartanburg flood products in the mountains and piedmont; no Topsail beach-weather line runs. USNO phases API answered this morning: new moon Saturday, Oct. 10, 15:50 UT, first quarter Oct. 18, 16:12 UT, full moon Oct. 26, 04:12 UT; the fetcher's waxing crescent, 1 percent, 1.0 days is the second day past the exact phase, spring tides. waters.read: 1340 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: Blown out. The read string is the fetcher's own verdict, "1340 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.", and the USGS two-day trace for 03186500, pulled at 5:48 a.m., says how it got there. The river sat at base flow all weekend, 45.3 to 48.8 cfs, and read 47.6 cfs and 1.28 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark; it crept over 50 at 9:45 a.m. Sunday (51.2), was 62.8 cfs and 1.40 feet at 1:45 p.m., and then went up in a wall: 128 cfs at 2 p.m., 809 and 3.49 feet at 2:15, 1,010 at 3 p.m., 1,530 at 4:45, 2,080 at 5:30, and a peak so far of 2,430 cfs and 5.51 feet at 7 and 7:15 p.m. Sunday, more than 50 times the morning's flow and more than four feet of stage. It has receded since, 2,060 at 10 p.m., 1,740 at midnight, 1,450 at 2 a.m., 1,340 at 3:45, and 1,320 to 1,340 cfs and 4.22 to 4.24 feet between 4 and 5:15 a.m., the fall flattening in the last hour. The fetcher's rising flags are right on the day: against the true 24-hour mark the river is up 1,292 cfs and 2.96 feet; its 48.8 and 1.29 comparison is the first point of its window, the 6 a.m. Saturday reading, not 24 hours ago, which is a one-step difference this morning and changes nothing. The same rain is in the Gauley: the Craigsville gauge above Summersville Lake (03189100) went from 198 cfs at 2 p.m. Sunday to a peak of 3,940 cfs and 13.57 feet at 2:45 a.m., 3,820 at 5:30, and the Gauley above Belva (03192000) peaked at 5,000 cfs and 5.38 feet at 1 a.m., 4,470 at 5 a.m., while 03189600 below the dam held 11.00 to 11.07 feet of stage all window, the release unchanged on the trace; readings of USGS traces, not Corps statements. NWS's active product list for West Virginia was empty at 5:48 a.m., no flood watch, warning or advisory on the Gauley, Elk or Williams. At 1,340 cfs the river is 28 times Sunday morning's flow and nearly three feet above it, the pocket water, the plunge pools and the undercuts all under one brown push, and there is no fly or leader to print for it. The fetcher's bank verdict stands; Sept. 22-23's high water took 19 days to recede to base flow, and the trace will say when this one is fishing.
waters.note: The fetcher's 48.8 cfs and 1.29 feet comparison point is the first point of its two-day window, the 6 a.m. Saturday reading, not 24 hours ago; the trace's true 24-hour mark is 47.6 cfs and 1.28 feet at 5:15 a.m. Sunday, Sunday's edition reading. The rising flags are right on the day (up 1,292 cfs and 2.96 feet) and the comparison error is one gauge step. The river left base flow at 2 p.m. Sunday (62.8 to 128 cfs), peaked at 2,430 cfs and 5.51 feet at 7-7:15 p.m. Sunday, and has fallen since to 1,320-1,340 cfs, flat in the last hour. No NWS flood product for West Virginia at 5:48 a.m. The Summersville release is read off USGS 03189600's stage trace (discharge series empty again) and 03192000's discharge trace, not from the Corps. WVDNR's trout stocking page was not opened today; no stocking line is printed.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.reading: 26.03 feet at 5 a.m., flagged rising against 24.53 in the fetcher's comparison.
waters.read: 26.0 ft and rising — normal pool. Ordinary bank access.
waters.working: Up nearly a foot on the day, and the rising flag is right on the day. The trace, pulled at 5:48 a.m., runs 25.09 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark and Sunday's edition reading, 25.41 at 8 a.m., 25.50 at 11, back to 25.07 at 6 p.m. through the lockage chop, then a steady climb from 7 p.m., 25.28 at 8, 25.53 at 10, 25.83 at midnight, 26.02 at 1 a.m., 26.05 at 2 and 3, 26.10 at 4, 26.15 at 4:15, the window's high, and 26.03 at 5 a.m. That is up 0.94 on the day, so the fetcher's flag is right there, and a 12-hundredth ease off the 4:15 high in the last 45 minutes, so the flag is soft at the hour. Its 24.53 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 6 a.m. Saturday reading (this morning's pull opens at 24.53), not 24 hours ago, and against it the rise looks like 1.50. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, normal pool, ordinary bank access. The water coming is Sunday's rain, not a release change: on the USGS traces the Gauley above Belva peaked at 5,000 cfs at 1 a.m. and read 4,470 at 5, up from 2,690 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the Gauley near Craigsville above the lake ran 174 cfs to 3,940 overnight, and 03189600 below Summersville Dam held 11.00 to 11.07 feet of stage all window; the Williams at Cowen, in the same hills, peaked at 2,430 cfs Sunday evening. Those are readings of USGS traces, not Corps statements; the Corps' Huntington District site was not opened, so no lake elevation and no Corps release figure is printed. With the Kanawha's tributaries that high overnight, this pool has more coming through the day. At 26.0 and rising on a pool, with a foot of new water and the color that comes with it, the river fishes the slack behind structure rather than the structure itself: shad are the forage and skipjack are with them, so a white or pearl swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon worked through the eddy behind each wing dam and along the downstream face of the riprap where the current breaks, a half-ounce blade bait on the inside of the creek mouths as they push dirty water into the main river, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the slack of the outside bends for the blues and flatheads after dark, a 1 percent moon leaving the water about as dark as it gets. The lock wall at Byrd is the deep edge for the sauger on a jigging spoon when the current eases. No NWS product covers Mason County at 5:48 a.m.

The rising flag is right on the day (up 0.94, not the 1.50 the comparison implies) and soft at the hour (26.15 at 4:15 a.m. the window high, 26.03 at 5). The Summersville release is read off USGS 03189600's stage trace and 03192000's discharge trace, not from the Corps.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam

waters.read: 28.0 ft and rising — up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Up nearly two feet on the day, and the rising flag is right on the day and right at the hour. The trace, pulled at 5:48 a.m., runs 26.07 at 5 a.m. Sunday, the true 24-hour mark and Sunday's edition reading, 26.44 at 10 a.m., 26.77 at 3 p.m., 26.97 at 7, 27.14 at 8, 27.32 at 11, 27.35 at midnight, 27.47 at 2 a.m., 27.64 at 3, 27.85 at 4 and 28.01 at 5 a.m., the window's high, with every hourly reading from 7 p.m. on higher than the one before. That is up 1.94 on the day and up 0.37 in the last two hours, so the fetcher's flag is right on both counts. Its 25.5 is the first point of its own two-day window, the 6 a.m. Saturday reading (this morning's pull opens at 25.51), not 24 hours ago, and against it the rise looks like 2.51. The read string is the fetcher's band verdict, up and pushing, expect colour and current, fish the slack behind anything solid. The Point Pleasant pool above has risen 0.94 on the day, the Gauley above Belva peaked at 5,000 cfs at 1 a.m. on the USGS trace and 03189600 below Summersville Dam is flat at 11.05 feet, a reading of the USGS traces and not a Corps statement, so what lifted this gauge overnight has a foot of pool and a Gauley crest still behind it, and the current below Byrd carries through the day. At 28.0 and rising with color, the fetcher's own line is the whole lure problem: the forage is shad and skipjack with crawfish in the riprap, so a white swimbait or a three-quarter-ounce spoon swum through the eddy below each wing dam where the pushed water slacks, a half-ounce blade bait or a chartreuse-and-white paddletail on a half-ounce head held in the seam behind the riprap points in low light, a black-and-blue jig for the smallmouth and the drum in the slack pockets of the rock where the fish tuck out of the push, and cut skipjack on the bottom in the barge cuts and the slack of the outside bends for the blues and the flatheads after dark, the night after the new moon still near the darkest of the month; the lock wall fishes from the downstream side on a live skipjack for the hybrids when the gates open. No NWS product covers Cabell or Wayne County at 5:48 a.m.

The rising flag is right on the day (up 1.94, not the 2.51 the comparison implies) and right at the hour (28.01 at 5 a.m. the window high).

waters.reading: Sound at Hampstead: low 3:57 AM at 0.5 ft, high 9:58 AM at 4.4 ft, low 4:36 PM at 0.8 ft, high 10:14 PM at 3.6 ft. Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: low 2:33 AM at 0.3 ft, high 9:02 AM at 5.6 ft, low 3:24 PM at 0.4 ft, high 9:20 PM at 4.3 ft. Water 73.4F at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, observed 5:36 a.m. Moon waxing crescent, 1% lit, 1.0 days old.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 9:58 AM and 10:14 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Second day past the new moon: the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered again this morning, puts the exact new moon at 15:50 UT Saturday, 11:50 a.m. ET, and the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 1 percent lit and 1.0 days old, so the spring tides are still on, big swings and hard inlet current, with the first quarter Oct. 18 and the full moon Oct. 26. The beach weather that ran the last two mornings is gone: NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender at 5:48 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no coastal flood advisory, and the five flood products active in North Carolina are all NWS Greenville-Spartanburg's in the mountains and piedmont. The sound at Hampstead came off a 0.5-foot low at 3:57 a.m. and fills 3.9 feet to a 4.4-foot high at 9:58 a.m.; it then drains 3.6 feet to a 0.8-foot low at 4:36 p.m., so the last two hours of the ebb, about 2:30 to 4:36 p.m., land in the afternoon, and fills 2.8 feet to a 3.6-foot high at 10:14 p.m., after dark; all four sound events fall inside Monday. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: low 2:33 a.m. at 0.3, high 9:02 a.m. at 5.6, low 3:24 p.m. at 0.4, high 9:20 p.m. at 4.3, a 5.3- and 5.2-foot swing against Sunday's 5.4 and 5.4. Today's lags from the two tables are 56 and 54 minutes on the highs and 84 and 72 minutes on the lows, against 52 and 49 and 80 and 72 on Sunday; the lows again lag longer than the highs, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 73.4 degrees at 5:36 a.m., down 0.2 from Sunday's 73.6 and 0.9 from Saturday's 74.3. What is running is 11 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:48 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings starting to show at the piers, and inshore red drum as the main target, scattered through the ICW, the creeks and the inlets, with no real word on trout; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, a few trout on early topwater, glass minnows thick off the beach; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout in the first hour of light on Spook Jrs. and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds on shrimp at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or Gulp under popping corks, flounder as bycatch; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small metal and epoxy jigs. The piers: Jolly Roger reports tons of bait, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem, and the first morning in three without a weather problem: the 9:58 a.m. high puts spring-tide water over the grass and up the dock pilings, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about 8 to 9:58 a.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the ebb, roughly 2:30 to 4:36 p.m., a daylight spring ebb with no flood watch over it: finger mullet and shrimp are the forage and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead; on the evening flood, 4:36 to 10:14 p.m., a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars as they cover, and the dock lights are the trout spot once the near-moonless dark sets in toward the 10:14 p.m. high, with the water at Beaufort two days into a slide under 74 and the report saying the trout turn on as it cools. The surf side, with no advisory on it today and 5.6 feet of water at the pier on the 9:02 a.m. high, is Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the morning flood and cut bait on the bottom for the slot reds in the evening, the pattern every pier in the report gives. Slack at 9:58 a.m., 4:36 p.m. and 10:14 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
